exposure: Mode of birth (C-section vs. vaginal delivery)
Disease modifying therapy decisions during gestation and postpartum
cohort: The study included 170 pregnant women with multiple sclerosis (wMS) participating in the Canadian Multiple Sclerosis Pregnancy Study (CANPREG-MS).
finding: The rate of C-sections was significantly higher in women with MS (37.1%) compared to the general Canadian population (28%), with most C-sections being performed for obstetrical indications rather than maternal MS.
mod_finding: C-sections were performed at an earlier gestational age than vaginal deliveries, but birthweight and MS relapse rates in the first month postpartum did not differ by mode of delivery.
followup_time: 1 month after C-section deliveries (for MS relapses)
birth_weight: Did not differ by mode of delivery.
gest_age: C-sections were performed at an earlier gestational age than vaginal deliveries.
